title: Probe orchestration and span provenance playbook
content:
Summary:

This working playbook describes a lightweight, operator-friendly approach to orchestrating synthetic probes for inference paths and attaching reliable span provenance metadata so investigation flows from dashboards -> traces -> root cause are fast and low-noise. Focus: probes that exercise token-paths (text gen), embedding endpoints, and cache-warmth scenarios.

Intent / non-goals:
- Intent: provide concrete metric contracts, span field definitions, and dashboard widgets for probe-driven SLI coverage.
- Non-goal: exhaustive tracing spec for every microcall. Keep spans small and provenance rich.

Key definitions (short):
- Probe: synthetic request that runs a defined scenario (prompt template + model + routing policy) aiming to exercise a signal (latency, kv-cache, cold-start).
- Probe orchestration: scheduling, routing, and versioning probes across regions/tiers with backpressure and cost limits.
- Span provenance: a minimal set of trace/span attributes that let operators answer who/what/why/when for a probe or user request.

Required span provenance fields (contract):
- probe.id: UUID for synthetic runs (present on root span).
- probe.scenario: short string (eg: prompt-short-context-8k).
- model.variant: model id + quantization tag (eg: gptx-13b-q4_0).
- route.policy: routing decision (primary|fallback|dedicated).
- tenant.id: multi-tenant tag (or 'sys' for infra probes).
- kv.cache.warmth: enum (cold|partial|warm) for inference spans when cache considered.
- prefix.bytes: integer, number of prefix tokens loaded into KV cache.
- batch.size: integer on any batching span.
- cpu/gpu: machine-type tag for quick capacity attribution.
- sample.weight: fraction used by sampling policy so replays can reweight events.

Metric contracts (SLI mapping):
- probe.latency.p95_ms: time from request-received to first-token for short prompts. Unit: ms. Aggregation: p95 over probe.scenario in 5m windows.
- probe.gen.tokens_per_sec: throughput for generation phases; helpful for throughput regressions.
- probe.kv.eviction_rate: per-model eviction events / minute for KV cache.
- probe.error.rate: percent non-200 responses or generation-aborts.
- probe.quality.regression: ratio of probe-eval quality checks failed (lightweight heuristics).
Measurement rules:
- Tag all metrics with model.variant and probe.scenario to enable slicing.
- Store probe.* metrics in short-term high-cardinality tier (7d) then rollup to 90d numeric aggregates.

Trace sampling & retention heuristics:
- Always keep 100% traces for probe.id.* when probe.error.rate > 0.5% in a window.
- Adaptive sampling: for normal probe runs keep 5% traces, but ensure at least 5 traces per scenario per hour retained.
- Redaction: PII must be removed at source; probes should never include realistic PII.

Probe orchestration patterns (ops-friendly):
1) Canary burst (deployment smoke): run N=50 probes across 3 regions in ramped cadence. Watch probe.latency.p95 and probe.error.rate.
2) Cache-warmth sweep: run three probe cohorts (cold/partial/warm) in sequence to measure delta. Use probe.id.parent to tie spans across the sweep.
3) Multi-model fanout: single probe triggers parallel requests to model variants to compare perf/quality. Use trace.group to link the fanout.

Dashboard notes / widget ideas (compact):
- Scenario heatmap (rows=scenario, cols=region): p95 latency colorized; mouseover shows probe.count and sample traces link.
- KV warmth delta bar: p95(cold) vs p95(warm) by model.variant.
- Probe quality sparkline: rolling 1h failure rate with annotation for deploys (linked via tag deploy.id).
- Trace probe explorer: quick filter by probe.scenario, model.variant, and probe.id; show span provenance columns (kv.cache.warmth, batch.size).
- Cost burn widget: estimated tokens generated for probes (tokens * model.cost_per_token) by scenario.

Operational runbook (quick):
- If probe.latency.p95 spikes > x2 baseline: open investigation -> filter traces by probe.scenario & region -> look for kv.cache.warmth and batch.size changes -> check recent rollouts (ENG-8421).
- If probe.error.rate climbs: ensure model.variant tag changed recently -> check fallback events in route.policy spans -> escalate to runtime oncall.

Implementation notes / pragmatic constraints:
- Keep span baggage small: string enums and small ints only; avoid large prompt payloads in spans (store prompt fingerprint hash).
- DB for probe metadata: keep lightweight registry (scenario -> owner, expected baseline, cost budget). This can live as a YAML in repo initially.
- Cost control: orchestration must apply token & invocation caps per scenario per day; default budget: $50/day across all probes for a team until approved.

Checklist before enabling a new probe scenario: 
- [ ] scenario owner assigned and contact in metadata
- [ ] baseline p50/p95 documented in registry
- [ ] cost budget assigned and cap configured
- [ ] span provenance fields added to tracing instrumentation
- [ ] dashboard widget proto created and reviewed by owner

Open questions / items for follow-up:
- Should probe.* metrics be routed to a separate telemetry sink for high-cardinality experiments? tradeoffs: cost vs iteration speed.
- Standardize a small controlled vocabulary for probe.scenario names (suggest: <intent>-<workload>-<len> eg: chat-short-ctx).
- Investigate automating probe-to-deploy link via CI pipeline so deploy.id auto-tags probe runs.

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Wire up ENG-8421 -> add adaptive sampler that promotes traces when a metric breaches SLO. (Jordan to pick up)
- Draft registry format and PR for observability repo (see linked GH PR).

Slack refs: #obs-probes, #runtime-alerts

End of playbook (working draft).

Acknowledgements: initial ideas from oncall rotation notes and the probe workshop (June 2025).
